conceptual assets.information: The operational enable setting determines whether the one-wire controller runs, whether its FIFOs are cleared, and whether the external clock generator is enabled. Controller operation depends on this state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a bus write changes the enable state at line 142 and the state controls operation at lines 199, 231, 258 and 311. Availability is at risk because clearing or disabling the setting can clear both FIFOs and stop clocked serial operation at lines 199, 231 and 258.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the enable bit through a bus write to disable the controller, clear queued transfers, or incorrectly enable it during an unintended operation.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and divider settings determine the timing of one-wire slots and serial engine progress. Correct one-wire transfers depend on these stored rate settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus writes replace the prescaler and divider at lines 144 and 145, changing the timing configuration. Availability is at risk because these settings control clock-source selection, the divider comparison and tick generation at lines 260-265, so an incorrect value can stall or mis-time transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write an incorrect prescaler or divider value so that one-wire slots are mistimed and transfers fail or stop progressing.

conceptual assets.information: A transmit FIFO entry combines a one-wire operation command with its associated eight-bit payload. The serial engine uses the queued entry to generate the one-wire transfer.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because bus-provided payload data is carried into the serial engine and can be exposed on the one-wire output at lines 328, 342 and 300-302. Integrity is at risk because a bus write supplies the transmit command and payload at line 201 and the serial engine uses them at lines 323-335. Availability is at risk because disabling or clearing the transmit FIFO at line 199, or failing to pop it through the control logic at lines 200 and 202, can withhold a required transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter or clear a queued command and payload, or observe the resulting one-wire waveform, causing an incorrect or missing external transaction.

conceptual assets.information: The sampled eight-bit value received from the one-wire device is assembled into a result and returned through the bus response. Software use of the peripheral depends on receiving the correct data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the received value is exposed through the bus response data at line 161. Integrity is at risk because samples from onewire_i enter at line 296, are assembled by the serial engine at line 352, and are returned at line 161, allowing a corrupted or spoofed wire signal to produce an incorrect result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the one-wire input while sampling so that software receives a false or attacker-chosen data byte.

conceptual assets.information: The presence result records whether a one-wire device responded during the reset and presence-detection sequence. Software reads this result as part of the received FIFO word.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the presence result is computed from the sampled one-wire input at line 375 and returned to software at line 162, so a manipulated response can falsely indicate device presence or absence.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the sampled one-wire level during presence detection so that software accepts a nonexistent device or rejects a valid one.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt indication reports that the controller is enabled, its transmit FIFO is empty, and the serial engine is not busy. System software may depend on this event to service or continue one-wire transfers.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because irq_o is generated from the enable, transmit FIFO and serial busy conditions at line 243, so altered controller state can cause a missing or spurious interrupt.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the enable or transfer state so that software receives a false interrupt or never receives the interrupt needed to service the peripheral.
